question: Should AXorcist be distributed as a standalone official Homebrew formula, and should that formula build tagged source or install release binaries?
rationale: Both approaches are technically plausible, but the choice determines whether AXorcist is an independently supported CLI, which repository owns packaging, and what release automation must be maintained.

options.title: Official source formula
options.body: Add an `openclaw/tap/axorcist` formula that builds tagged source with Swift and coordinate its version updates with AXorcist releases.

options.title: Official binary formula
options.body: First publish versioned macOS release archives and checksums, then have the official tap install those artifacts for faster, toolchain-free installation.

options.title: Route users to Peekaboo
options.body: Decline a standalone formula and document Peekaboo as the supported Homebrew-distributed CLI for higher-level macOS automation.

recommendation.title: Official source formula
recommendation.body: Add an `openclaw/tap/axorcist` formula that builds tagged source with Swift and coordinate its version updates with AXorcist releases.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest observed connection to AXorcist package maintenance, releases, and the surrounding Peekaboo distribution surface.
